## Summary

Set up a complete failover routing chain in the proxy where requests try Qwen3 locally first, then fall back to OpenCode Zen free tier (deepseek-v4-flash-free), then OpenCode Go (deepseek-v4-flash). Configure Pi to connect to this proxy and use the failover model.

## User Story

As a developer using the LLM proxy, I want to send a single request and have it automatically try local Qwen3 first. If no slots are available, fall back to a free remote model. If that is rate-limited, fall back to a paid remote model.

## Context

- The proxy config entry `qwen3-fallback` was partially added in `proxy/config.yaml` with three providers (local-qwen3, opencode-deepseek-free, opencode-go-deepseek)
- `proxy/proxy_remote.py` was modified to support the `model` field for upstream model name override
- A bug exists in `proxy/proxy/ui.py` where `_extract_router_model_ids` is called without being imported (NameError)
- Pi needs to be configured to connect to the proxy with the failover model as available

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError bug in `ui.py` is fixed
2. The proxy reloads successfully with the `qwen3-fallback` model entry
3. A request to `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: qwen3-fallback` returns a response (from whichever provider succeeds)
4. The response includes an `X-Provider` header identifying which provider served the request
5. Pi is configured to use the proxy with the failover model as one of its available models
6. All existing tests still pass
data.title: Complete failover plan configuration with Pi instance integration

# KV-cache memory accounting per config

## Summary

Measure or estimate memory per slot (KV cache + overhead) at each configuration of the ctx-size evaluation (parent LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM): 8×32.8K, 6×43.7K, 4×65.5K, 3×87.4K, 2×131K. Verify or correct the unverified "~71GB available" claim from the original intake and produce a headroom table.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Per-slot KV-cache memory recorded at each of the five configurations, sourced from llama-server (`/props`, admin metrics) and/or `rocm-smi` GPU metrics, with the measurement method stated.
2. The "~71GB available" claim is verified or corrected with concrete evidence (rocm-smi / admin metrics captured during benchmark runs).
3. A headroom table is produced: per-slot memory, total memory at peak slot usage, and headroom vs. measured available memory, for each config.
4. Findings are recorded in the parent work item LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Collect rocm-smi + llama-server memory metrics during the F2/F3 run windows (no extra restarts needed).
2. Compute per-slot and total KV memory per config; cross-check against `local_model_ctx_size` expectations.
3. Build the headroom table and document the memory measurement evidence.

## Dependencies

- F3 (Candidate benchmarks) — uses its run windows; also consumes F2 baseline memory snapshots.

## Deliverables

- Memory accounting table + verification/correction of the ~71GB claim.

Implements the `available_times` feature (LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC) on the live config: add `available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]` (UTC, end-exclusive) to every `deepseek-v4-flash` direct provider entry (`provider: deepseek`, endpoint api.deepseek.com). Such entries exist in the `plan`, `author`, and `code` fallback chains — all three hit the same DeepSeek API and must be timed for the restriction to be effective.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] All `deepseek-v4-flash` direct-provider entries (plan/author/code) carry the off-peak `available_times` windows
- [ ] Config still parses (yaml validation passes); no other provider is timed

# Raise cold-cache context routing threshold (recapture 30-39.6K band for local)

## Problem statement

Overnight proxy analysis (2026-08-11, window 01:00-11:13, 3,145 requests) shows context-driven fallbacks are the #2 remote-use driver: `context_too_large` 269 (16.7%) + `large_context_bypass` 251 (15.6%) = 520 events (~32% of 1,608 fallbacks). The effective per-slot routing clamp is only ~39,595 tokens (`local_model_ctx_size 131072 // 3 slots - 4096 output headroom`), so any prompt over ~39.6K bypasses local entirely.

`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold: 30000` is an ECONOMIC new-token threshold (LP-0MRCSSBTM002NK3B): when the slot cache is cold and estimated prompt tokens exceed it, local routing is bypassed. Prompts in the 30,000-39,595 band with a cold cache currently go remote even though they FIT the KV slot. Raising the threshold toward the warm clamp (which is itself clamped to the per-slot context, LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1) recaptures that band for local compute.

Goal: route more cold-cache mid-size prompts local; reduce context-driven remote fallbacks without changing slot count or KV capacity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` raised in a MODE-AWARE way (a single config value cannot serve both modes — cheap-mode warm resolves to 100000, fast-mode to ~39594): fast config 30000→38000, cheap config 30000→60000 — CHEAP LATER REVERTED to 30000 per data-backed REVERT (child LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K AC7; 3/4 nights at 60000 breached guardrails); post-revert analysis (2026-08-19/20 cheap windows) supports raising cheap to 38000 (same as fast) as the safe symmetric value — see producer decision 2026-08-20. (or an implementation deriving cold from the active per-slot ctx). Each value verified to stay BELOW that mode's effective warm threshold so the (cold, warm] band never collapses (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP dead-code guard); `validate_local_routing_config` passes.
2. Routing decision unchanged for prompts > per-slot clamp (still `context_too_large` bypass — physical capacity, never routed local).
3. Existing router tests updated/added: a cold-cache prompt at e.g. 35K tokens now routes local; a cold-cache prompt at 45K still bypasses; the band-collapse validation still passes with the new value (in both modes).
4. `local_model_ctx_size` unchanged (131072) — no slot/ctx rebalancing in this item.
5. Full test suite passes (quiet mode) + a post-change overnight/24h proxy report confirms the context-fallback share dropped (compare against the 2026-08-11 baseline).
6. Cheap-mode queue guardrails hold post-change (see child validation item): nightly `contention_fallback_after_queue_count` stays < ~2x baseline (baseline max 115) and sampled `contention_queue_depth` max stays < 4 sustained.

## Cheap-mode dimension (added 2026-08-13 — overnight headroom analysis)

The same economic question applies to the CHEAP window (01:00–10:00, 2 slots x 262144): there the effective per-slot clamp is ~126,976 and the warm threshold resolves to the config value 100000 (min(100000, 262144//2 − 4096)), so the (cold, warm] band is (30000, 100000]. Verified in proxy logs: cheap-hour `routing_skip_local` lines log `cold_threshold=30000 warm_threshold=100000`; fast-hour lines log `warm_threshold=39594`.

Aug 12–13 cheap-window analysis (routing_skip_local decisions): 476 `context_too_large` + 215 `large_context_bypass`. Of the 215, 101 had new_tokens in (30K, 60K] (~50/night) and 197 in (30K, 90K]. Raising cold to 60K (cheap mode) recaptures ~50 cold-cache requests/night for local. A further 66 requests had estimated 100–127K (would flip if warm config raised to ~127K; smaller win, optional).

**Headroom / risk (sized before recommending):**
- Contention queue (cheap, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D): sampled depth 0 in 87% of /v1/status polls, max observed 3 (cap 4) — never hit the cap in samples.
- Queue outcomes per night: Aug 12 — 83 queued, 34 overflowed (59% served local); Aug 13 — 59 queued, 18 overflowed (69% served). Overflow events (`fallback_after_queue`) 115 → 17 per night.
- Local backend is busy often: `available_slots=0` in 4,398 of 7,578 status samples (58%) across the two windows — NOT idle. Flipped requests will frequently queue; the flip is latency-bounded (max wait 60s) and degrades gracefully (falls back to remote on timeout — same outcome as today, +<=60s latency).
- Net estimate: ~50/night flipped, ~59–69% served local → ~30/night net local gain; contention-queue arrivals roughly double in peak hours (01–02, 07–08), overflow roughly doubles in absolute terms (still tens/night).

**Recommendation (mode-aware, UPDATED 2026-08-20 after revert + post-revert data):**
- CHEAP mode: initial bump to 60000 was REVERTED to 30000 (child LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K AC7 — guardrails failed 3/4 nights at 60000: contention_fallback_after_queue 315/335/180 vs 2x baseline 230, sustained depth-4). Post-revert cheap windows at 30000 all pass (fa Δ 0/4/38 ≤ 230; no sustained depth-4). **Safe re-raise target: 38000** (same as fast/default — one symmetric band; proven safe in fast mode with zero sustained guardrail events; 38K < cheap warm 100K and < boot clamp 61,440). 42000 is the aggressive maximum (monitor-gated); ≥46000 proven-risky.
- FAST mode: keep the original 30000→38000 bump (band (38K, 39.6K] stays non-empty — LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP dead-code guard); zero guardrail events observed Aug 13-20.
- Guardrail: cold must stay < effective warm in EACH mode; validate with `validate_local_routing_config`.

## Notes / related

- **Compaction is the companion lever** (30 sessions were >=80% of per-slot context; `context_pressure_warn_ratio: 0.8` warns but agents' compaction cadence is the real control). Out of scope here — agent-side, tracked separately if needed.
- Tokenizer caveat (LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ / LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM): the `plan`/`code`/`author` chains already use the native `qwen3` tokenizer, so estimates for these models are Qwen3-exact — the tiktoken 1.69x undercount caveat applies only to chains without `tokenizer: qwen3`.
- This item is in the llm (llama-proxy) worklog; the herdr-side slot-utilization levers are tracked in the ContextHub worklog.

## Key Files
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml`
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_mode_config.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_per_slot_ctx.py`
- `docs/llama-router.md`
- `proxy/README.md`
data.title: Raise local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold 30000 -> ~38000 to route more cold-cache prompts local

## Problem

Discovered from 2026-08-12 12h audit analysis. On 2026-08-11 23:42 an audit of LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D was launched from the wrong project context (SorraAgents cwd instead of llm). Consequences (audit-LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D-20260811-234211.log):

1. Debug logs written to ~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/ (wrong project dir).
2. All 5 child audit persists failed: "wl audit-set failed (rc=1): Work item not found: LP-0MSOZESW90057SRR" etc. — swallowed as warnings.
3. Phase 2 deep analysis ran against the WRONG FILE SCOPE — the audit skill own manifest (skill/audit/ root: audit_pr.py, __init__.py, SKILL.md; scripts/: audit_runner.py, persist_audit.py, scan.py, cleanup_debug_logs.py, __init__.py; tests/: 11 files). Every AC returned "unmet" with evidence like "proxy/provider.py ... is not listed in the FILE SCOPE manifest" and "Work item LP-0MSOZESW90057SRR could not be resolved via wl search (0 results)".

Cost: ~124 min model time + ~92 min wall clock completely wasted; forced the full R2 re-audit (~179 min model time). A mis-scoped audit is indistinguishable from a failed audit and MUST fail fast instead of producing a misleading "Ready to close: No" with all-unmet verdicts.

## Goal

Audit runs verify their launch context (worklog, owning project, FILE SCOPE manifest) before spending model time; any mismatch aborts loudly and early.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. audit_runner.py verifies the resolved worklog/project owns the work item before Phase 1; a mismatch (e.g. launched from a non-owning cwd) produces a clear error and non-zero exit, never a full run.
2. The Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest is validated to contain the work item repository files; if the resolved scope is the audit skill own tree (or lacks the item repo), the run aborts with a scope error instead of emitting "unmet" verdicts.
3. Child audit persistence failures ("Work item not found") are fatal (abort run, non-zero exit) rather than swallowed as warnings that lead to a misleading parent report.
4. Tests: (a) launching from a non-owning project dir fails fast with zero pi calls; (b) a scope manifest missing the item repo aborts before Phase 2; (c) child persist failure aborts the run.
5. Regression check: a correctly-configured audit (like LP-0MSLSR7NU005R03D, 19 min clean pass) still runs unchanged.

## Users


- **Operators / agents launching audits** — expect a mis-scoped launch to fail fast (seconds, no pi calls) with a clear error, never a full wasted run.
- **Agents consuming audit verdicts** — expect every persisted verdict to be trustworthy; child-persist failures must not be silently swallowed into a misleading parent report.
- **Audit maintainers** — need the guard covered by regression tests so correctly-configured audits keep running unchanged.

User stories:

- "As an agent launching an audit, I want to be told immediately when I launched from the wrong project directory, so I don't waste ~2–3 hours of model time on a doomed run."
- "As an operator reviewing an audit report, I want child persistence failures to abort the run, so I never read a parent report whose children were never actually persisted."
- "As a maintainer, I want the guard to be zero-cost for correct launches, so my 19-minute clean audit still runs unchanged."


- Guard must run before any pi/model calls (fail fast) — AC4(a) requires zero pi calls.
- Implementation targets the audit skill in the **SorraAgents** repo (`skill/audit/`), installed at `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/`; work item tracked in the `llm` worklog.
- Exit codes must be non-zero and messages clear enough to distinguish scope errors from genuine audit failures.
- Correctly-configured launches must incur negligible overhead (regression AC5).
- Do not change the persisted-report format or the audit skill's public CLI flags.

## Existing state


- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`cmd_issue`, ~line 4223) resolves the item via `_run_wl(["wl", "show", issue_id, "--json"])` (~line 4404) and starts Phase 1 regardless of cwd; worklog resolution is delegated to `_resolve_worklog_flags` / `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix` (shared helper) with explicit-dir > prefix-sibling-scan > cwd-chain precedence.
- `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT = _detect_project_root()` (git root or cwd) is computed at import time and is cwd-dependent — a wrong cwd silently produces a wrong project scope.
- Phase 2 builds the FILE SCOPE manifest via `_build_file_scope_manifest` (~line 2190); when the audit skill's own tree is resolved, the manifest contains the skill files (audit_pr.py, SKILL.md, scripts/, tests/) instead of the audited repo's files.
- Child audit persistence uses `persist_audit()` (`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`); failures (rc=1 "Work item not found") are currently logged as warnings, allowing a misleading parent report.
- Incident: 2026-08-11 audit of LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D launched from SorraAgents cwd → debug logs in `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/`, 5 child persists failed, Phase 2 ran against the skill's own manifest, all ACs "unmet"; ~124 min model time + ~92 min wall clock wasted.

## Desired change


- Add a launch-context guard early in `cmd_issue` (before Phase 1): resolve the worklog/project and verify ownership of the audited work item; on mismatch, print a clear error and exit non-zero with no pi calls.
- Validate the Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest before deep analysis: if it resolves to the audit skill's own tree or lacks the item's repo files, abort with a scope error.
- Promote child `persist_audit`/`wl audit-set` failures to fatal (abort run, non-zero exit).
- Add regression tests per AC4 and verify AC5 against a clean reference audit.

## Key Files:


- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — add launch-context guard before Phase 1 (in `cmd_issue` around the `wl show` resolution); validate FILE SCOPE manifest before Phase 2; make child persist failures fatal.
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — child audit persistence path; surface "Work item not found" as a fatal error rather than a warning.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document the fail-fast launch contract (wrong project/worklog/file-scope).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — new tests: (a) non-owning cwd fails fast with zero pi calls, (b) scope manifest missing item repo aborts before Phase 2, (c) child persist failure aborts; plus regression coverage for correct launches.

## Risks & assumptions


- **Risk:** the guard is too strict and blocks legitimate cross-project audits (e.g. an audit launched intentionally from another repo). Mitigation: ownership check uses the shared worklog-resolution precedence (explicit `--worklog-dir` wins); only a *mismatch* aborts, and the error message states the resolved vs expected project so operators can re-launch with the correct flag.
- **Risk:** child-persist-failure promotion to fatal could abort runs on transient `wl` hiccups. Mitigation: scope the fatal path to genuine "Work item not found" / audit-set rc!=0 errors, mirroring existing retry behaviour; document in SKILL.md.
- **Risk:** manifest validation falsely flags a correct scope (e.g. mono-repo items whose files legitimately live in the skill tree). Mitigation: validate that the item repo's tracked files are present in the manifest, not that the manifest equals the item repo.
- **Assumption:** "owning project" is derivable from the worklog prefix/sibling scan already implemented (shared `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`); no new config needed.
- **Assumption:** regression baseline LP-0MSLSR7NU005R03D remains a valid clean reference at implementation time.
- **Scope-creep guard:** performance tuning of Phase 2 (LP-0MSQ32WM5000NCB7), child-verdict reuse (LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR), and timeout elimination (LP-0MSQ32S2M001EA74) are tracked as separate items — do not fold them into this fix.

## Related work (curated)


- LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR — Audit runner: reuse fresh child audits in parent audits (child verdict reuse) — sibling audit-runner improvement (child handling).
- LP-0MSQ32WM5000NCB7 — Audit runner: cheaper/faster Phase 2 deep analysis (model override + evidence scope) — sibling audit-runner improvement (Phase 2).
- LP-0MSQ32S2M001EA74 — Audit runner: eliminate 30-min timeout waste (scale per-call budget + early-stall abort) — in-progress sibling; touches audit-runner call budget.
- LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D — the audit whose mis-scoped run triggered this item (completed).
- LP-0MSLSR7NU005R03D — clean 19-min reference audit used for the regression check (AC5).
- SA-0MSG48MEI0083K82 — audit runner worklog resolution fix referenced in audit_runner.py (non-project cwd).
- docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md — launch → monitor → abort contract for the runner.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers


Intake was **auto-completed** (work item description was already sufficiently defined: headline + Problem + Goal + 5 measurable ACs + concrete file/test sketch, `bug` type). No clarifying questions were required.

- Q: (none) — Answer: n/a — Source: auto-complete per intake skill evaluation heuristics (small `bug` with explicit ACs + implementation sketch).
- Research summary: inspected `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (cmd_issue ~L4223, `wl show` resolution ~L4404, `_build_file_scope_manifest` ~L2190, `_resolve_worklog_flags`/`_detect_project_root` L504–595), `persist_audit.py` child-persist path, `skill/audit/tests/` (11 test files incl. `test_audit_runner_worklog_dir.py`), and SKILL.md launch contract. Verified sibling audit-runner work items in the `llm` worklog. Implementation repo: SorraAgents `skill/audit/` (installed at `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88** – Log client IP in proxy status_request structured log for poller attribution (completed)
- **LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR** – Audit runner: reuse fresh child audits in parent audits (child verdict reuse) (open)
- **LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM** – Evaluate increasing local context size (ctx-size) to serve >65K-token prompts locally (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-audit-runner-launch-context-guard-LP-0MSQ32HNR007AI6B.md` — matched: 0mslsr7nu005r03d, 0msorqvk50012q4d, 124, 2026, abort (+115 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 124, 179, 2026, abort, acceptance (+109 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: 124, 179, 2026, abort, acceptance (+109 more)
data.title: Audit runner: launch-context guard (fail fast on wrong project/worklog/file scope)

# Proxy usage report: percentages in Total/Fast/Cheap columns should be category-relative

Headline: The proxy usage report's breakdown percentages (fallback reasons, routing-skip reasons, per-model, and the Session summary "Fallback events" row) currently use wrong denominators in the Fast/Cheap columns — each percentage must be relative to its own category (Total = across both buckets; Fast = fast-only; Cheap = cheap-only).

## Problem statement

In `report.md` produced by the proxy-usage-analysis skill, percentage values in the Total/Fast/Cheap columns of breakdown tables are computed against the wrong denominators. In the **Fallback reasons** and **routing_skip_local reasons** tables the Fast/Cheap percentages show each value's share of its *own row* (fast + cheap sum to 100% — i.e. "the fast/cheap split of this one reason"), not the reason's share *within* each category. The Session summary's **Fallback events** row and the **Per-model breakdown** have the same problem (fast/cheap shown as shares of all fallbacks / of that model's sessions). Operators therefore cannot directly compare how a reason or model affects fast vs cheap sessions.

## Users

Primary user: the operator (rgardler) reading the daily report (and the cron-generated archives in `~/proxy-usage-reports/`) to decide slot-schedule, ctx-size and routing-threshold changes.

User stories:
- As an operator, I want to see that `context_too_large` accounts for 60.3% of *fast* fallbacks but only 32.8% of *cheap* fallbacks (rather than a 90.0%/10.0% split of the reason itself), so I can judge whether the slot schedule under-serves one period.
- As an operator, I want the Session summary "Fallback events" row to show the fallback *rate within each category* (fast events ÷ fast requests, cheap events ÷ cheap requests), like-for-like with the Total column, so fast and cheap are comparable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Fallback reasons table** — for each reason row: `Fast` shows `fast_count (fast_count ÷ total-fast-fallback-events %)` and `Cheap` shows `cheap_count (cheap_count ÷ total-cheap-fallback-events %)`; the `% of fallbacks` column stays `count ÷ all fallback events`. Worked example from the 2026-08-16 report (fast_fb=5260, cheap_fb=1076): `context_too_large | 3526 | 55.7% | 3173 (60.3%) | 353 (32.8%)` (previously `3173 (90.0%) | 353 (10.0%)`).
2. **routing_skip_local reasons table** — same rule: `Fast` ÷ total fast routing-skips, `Cheap` ÷ total cheap routing-skips; `% of skips` column unchanged. Worked example from the 2026-08-16 report (fast skips=3211, cheap skips=176): `context_too_large | 3375 | 99.6% | 3200 (99.7%) | 175 (99.4%)`.
3. **Session summary "Fallback events" row** — `Fast` = fast fallback events ÷ fast requests, `Cheap` = cheap fallback events ÷ cheap requests; Total stays events ÷ all requests. Worked example: `6336 (65.4%) | 5260 (67.7%) | 1076 (56.3%)` (previously `5260 (83.0%) | 1076 (17.0%)`).
4. **Per-model breakdown** — `Fast` = this model's fast sessions ÷ total fast sessions, `Cheap` = this model's cheap sessions ÷ total cheap sessions. Worked example: `local | Qwen3 | 163 | 143 (69.8%) | 20 (27.0%)` with 205 fast / 74 cheap sessions (previously `143 (87.7%) | 20 (12.3%)`).
5. **Testing/validation** — unit/e2e tests updated to assert the category-relative denominators, including a mixed fast/cheap fixture where the new percentages differ from the old ones (fast + cheap no longer sum to 100% per row); report output regenerated from fixtures reads correctly.
6. **Documentation** — `SKILL.md`'s "% semantics" description ("every fast/cheap count carries its share of the metric's total") is updated to the category-relative rule.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Consistency property:** per-category reason percentages will sum to ~100% across all reasons within each category (since both numerator and denominator come from the same per-bucket counters) — a useful smoke check for tests; verify it holds for the mixed fixture.
- **Reader familiarity risk:** operators used to the old "fast/cheap split of the reason" semantics may misread the new numbers; mitigated by the SKILL.md update and keeping the `% of fallbacks` column as the total-relative anchor.
- **Scope-creep risk:** recommendation evidence strings and the share-of-total distribution rows are adjacent but intentionally unchanged; if the operator later wants them category-relative too, that is a separate work item (recorded in Constraints, not implemented here).
- **Assumption:** display-only change; no CSV/JSON/log-parse/bucketing behavior changes, verified by keeping those code paths untouched.

## Constraints

- **Out of scope — keep as-is:** distribution rows in the Session summary (Sessions, Requests, Dispatch denied fast/cheap shares of the total) remain share-of-total; the `% of fallbacks` / `% of skips` total columns remain unchanged; recommendation evidence strings (`Fast X (y%) / Cheap Z (w%)` in `recommendations.py`) keep their within-group split semantics; CSV outputs and the JSON summary are unchanged.
- Follow the existing `_pct(part, total)` helper and the already-computed `fast_fb` / `cheap_fb` sums in `reporting.py`; add an equivalent sum for routing skips rather than recomputing inline.
- No change to log parsing, bucketing, or aggregation — display-only change in the report renderer.

## Existing state

`reporting.py` (`build_report`) renders the following with incorrect category denominators:

- **Session summary, Fallback events row** (~L323-325): `fast_fb (fast_fb ÷ total fallbacks %)` / `cheap_fb (cheap_fb ÷ total fallbacks %)` — should be ÷ fast requests / ÷ cheap requests.
- **Fallback reasons table** (~L345-351): `d (d ÷ count %)` / `n (n ÷ count %)` where `count` is the row's own total — should be `d ÷ fast_fb` / `n ÷ cheap_fb`.

data.description:
# Serve cached per-slot detail when /slots counts are stale (slots_stale)

## Context

Cross-repo pair with the herdr downtime dispatcher (ContextHub WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F), which consumes `GET /llama/local/status`.

## Problem

When the fresh llama-server `/slots` query fails (e.g. HTTP 500 during a model reload or while generating), `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` degrades gracefully for the COUNTS — it serves the last-known `(available_slots, total_slots)` and sets `slots_stale: true` (LP-0MSVP7XJ6008QPKX). But the per-slot detail is queried separately via `_query_slots_detail(...)` and returned as `slots: []` on failure. Consumers therefore receive valid counts with NO per-slot identity.

Observed live (2026-09-24):

```json
{"active_query":true,"local_active_query":true,"model_switch_in_progress":false,"current_model":"Qwen3","llama_server_running":true,"available_slots":1,"total_slots":3,"slots_stale":true,"slots":[],"local_owner_session_id":["http://localhost:8080","audit-…"],"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds":645.5}
```

herdr now falls back safely (WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F), but per-slot identity is lost — same-slot idle tracking and the canonical spare-capacity gate degrade to the count-based path. Serving the cached detail restores identity.

## Fix

`observability.py` already maintains `_last_slot_details_cache` (updated by `_periodic_broadcast_loop()`, and already used as a fallback by `status_events()` in `proxy.ui`). The status handler does not use it. When the fresh `_query_slots_detail` fails or returns empty, fall back to `_last_slot_details_cache` (mirroring the counts fallback), and mark `slots_stale` when served slot data came from cache.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the fresh per-slot detail query fails and the cache is non-empty, the status payload serves the cached per-slot detail.
2. `slots_stale` is true whenever served slot data came from cache (counts or detail).
3. An empty/missing cache still yields `slots: []` — never a malformed payload.
4. A test pins the fallback for cache hit / miss / stale, and the endpoint still responds within the `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` budget.

## Notes

- Unblocks the strongest form of herdr WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F (per-slot identity preserved). herdr already falls back safely, so this is defence-in-depth rather than a hard blocker.
- Cross-repo: ContextHub RCA WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.
- The proxy-side lease semantics are referenced from herdr's `LOCAL_DISPATCH_LEASE_MAX_SECONDS` (default 1500 s) in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`.
data.title: llama-proxy: serve cached per-slot detail when /slots counts are stale (slots_stale) so herdr per-slot dispatch keeps slot identity
